# package auth

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-openadr/auth"
```

Package auth holds what the VTN needs to authenticate and authorize a request: the identity behind a bearer token and the OAuth2 scopes of OpenADR 3.

A VTN is given a Validator and does not issue tokens itself. Issuer is a small in-memory OAuth2 client-credentials token service for tests, examples and self-contained deployments; a production VTN would normally put a Validator in front of its own identity provider instead.

## Constants

```go
const (
	// ScopeReadAll lets Business Logic read every object.
	ScopeReadAll = "read_all"
	// ScopeReadTargets lets a VEN read programs and events, those with
	// targets only when the VEN has been granted matching targets.
	ScopeReadTargets = "read_targets"
	// ScopeReadVENObjects lets a VEN read the objects whose clientID is its own.
	ScopeReadVENObjects     = "read_ven_objects"
	ScopeWritePrograms      = "write_programs"
	ScopeWriteEvents        = "write_events"
	ScopeWriteReports       = "write_reports"
	ScopeWriteSubscriptions = "write_subscriptions"
	ScopeWriteVENs          = "write_vens"
)
```

OAuth2 scopes defined by OpenADR 3.1.0.

## Variables

```go
var ErrInvalidToken = errors.New("auth: invalid token")
```

ErrInvalidToken is returned by a Validator for a token that is unknown, malformed or expired. The VTN answers it with 401; any other error from a Validator is answered with 500.

### type Issuer

```go
type Issuer struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Issuer is an in-memory OAuth2 token service for the client-credentials grant (RFC 6749 section 4.4). It is the token endpoint as an http.Handler and the matching Validator. Tokens are opaque and are lost on restart.

An Issuer is safe for concurrent use.

#### func NewIssuer

```go
func NewIssuer(cfg IssuerConfig) (*Issuer, error)
```

NewIssuer returns an Issuer for the given clients.

#### func (Issuer) ServeHTTP

```go
func (is *Issuer) ServeHTTP(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request)
```

ServeHTTP is the token endpoint. Client credentials are taken from HTTP Basic authentication or from the client\_id and client\_secret form fields.

### type JWTConfig

```go
type JWTConfig struct {
	// Keys are keys to verify signatures with. See JWTKey.
	Keys []JWTKey
	// JWKSURL is where the identity provider publishes its signing keys as a
	// JSON Web Key Set (RFC 7517). Its keys are used in addition to Keys,
	// and fetched again when a token names a key that is not known.
	JWKSURL string
	// HTTPClient fetches the key set; a client with a 10 second timeout
	// when nil.
	HTTPClient *http.Client

	// Issuer, when set, is the iss a token must have.
	Issuer string
	// Audiences, when set, are the audiences this VTN answers to: the aud
	// of a token must name one of them. Set it whenever the identity
	// provider issues tokens for other services too.
	Audiences []string
	// ClientIDClaim names the claim that identifies the client. When empty,
	// the first of client_id, azp and sub that the token has.
	ClientIDClaim string
	// ScopeClaim names the claim that holds the scopes: a string of scopes
	// separated by spaces, or an array of them. When empty, scope, then scp.
	ScopeClaim string
	// Leeway is how far the clock of the issuer may differ; none when zero.
	Leeway time.Duration
	// Now replaces the clock, for tests.
	Now func() time.Time
}
```

JWTConfig configures a JWTValidator.

### type JWTKey

```go
type JWTKey struct {
	// ID is the kid of the tokens the key signs. A key without an ID is
	// tried for tokens without a kid, and for every token when it is the
	// only key.
	ID string
	// Key is an *rsa.PublicKey, an *ecdsa.PublicKey, an ed25519.PublicKey,
	// or a []byte holding the secret of an HMAC.
	//
	// The kind of key decides which algorithms it verifies: a public key is
	// never used as an HMAC secret, whatever the token claims.
	Key any
}
```

JWTKey is a key to verify token signatures with.

### type JWTValidator

```go
type JWTValidator struct {

	// fetched are the keys of the key set, by kid.

	// fetchErr is why the last fetch failed, while no key set was had.

}
```

JWTValidator is a Validator for bearer tokens that are JSON Web Tokens (RFC 7519) signed by an identity provider: the usual form of an OAuth2 access token.

It verifies the signature (RS256/384/512, ES256/384/512, EdDSA with Ed25519, HS256/384/512), requires an expiry that has not passed, honours nbf, and checks iss and aud as configured. A token without a signature is never accepted.

A JWTValidator is safe for concurrent use.

#### func NewJWTValidator

```go
func NewJWTValidator(cfg JWTConfig) (*JWTValidator, error)
```

NewJWTValidator returns a validator for cfg. It does not fetch the key set: that happens with the first token that needs it.

#### func (JWTValidator) Validate

```go
func (v *JWTValidator) Validate(ctx context.Context, token string) (Identity, error)
```

Validate implements Validator. Every way a token can be wrong is ErrInvalidToken; an error that is not means the key set could not be had.

### type Validator

```go
type Validator interface {

}
```

Validator resolves a bearer token to the identity it was issued to. Implementations must be safe for concurrent use.
